To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) non-commutative Yang-Mills theory can be defined on a commutative space, and (b) UV/IR mixing is not a fundamental property of non-commutative field theory, and can be avoided by introducing a suitable IR damping mechanism.

non-commutative Yang-Mills theory can be formulated as a non-local theory in the sense that the non-locality of the action is due to the presence of a new type of non-commutative field, the soft-breaking field, and that, as a consequence of this new field, the UV/IR mixing problem can be avoided.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of non-perturbative models for non-commutatve field theories which avoid UV/IR mixing problems.
the study of the infrared behavior of gauge theories in the presence of non-commutative space-time.
the study of the properties of the non-commutative (NC) U(N) Yang-Mills theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work provides a viable alternative to the Seiberg-Witten map, which is not based on a deformation of the commutative gauge field action, but instead on a generalized version of the latter.

the present model provides a viable framework for the construction of non-commutative Yang-Mills theory, in the sense that all the problems related to the UV/IR mixing are solved, and that the model can be used to study the non-commutative QCD in the large-N limit.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present approach to non-commutaive gauge field theories is based on the following ideas: (1) a non-commutative space-time is defined as an ordinary commutative space-time endowed with a non-commutativity parameter; (2) the gauge fields are treated as operators in the algebra generated by the non-commutative coordinates; (3) a generalized version of the non-commutativity relation is used to define the non-commutativeness of the gauge fields; (4)
we are now able to construct a consistent non-commutative version of the Gribov-Zwaniger approach to Yang-Mills theory.
the present approach provides an alternative method to the well-established Seiberg-Witten map, which has been used to construct the non-commutative version of the standard model, for instance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-commutative Yang-Mills theory is a UV complete theory.
the UV/IR mixing problem is not an obstacle to the formulation of a consistent non-commutative field theory.
the non-commutative action for U(N)-gauge fields can be written down in a manifestly U(N)-genuine form.
